column1: # Pokemon Pokopia (Switch 2, update v655360). Plays on the Mac
# Koei Tecmo's KTGL (KTSL2 sound), SDK 20.5.25 built for the Switch 2 (Ounce), NVN2. Modules main + subsdk0 (NintendoSDK_movie: WebM movies) + sdk.
# Packed from a dump folder (base/exefs, updates/<version>/) with scripts/pack_dump.py. RomFS: the newer RDB of ROMANCE OF THE THREE KINGDOMS 8 REMAKE under motor_asset_re/KIDS_PLATFORM_OUNCE
# v655360 is the update's title version; a dump has no control data to name a display version
# The Switch 2 leaves games 9 GB of its 12 GB (Donkey Kong Bananza's figure, not measured here). The NPDM declares no system resource (META +0x14 = 0): no virtual address memory.
# 256 MB in front + 256 MB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 9 GB heap region
# nninitStartup asks for pool - used memory and does not check the answer; the rewritten modules take 82 MB, more than the default 64 MB SetHeapSize checks the request against
# the game sets near = 0 (the log's depth mode line): the pipeline bases made before it runs are made for that mode
# pointer look (hle_hid.c): the camera turns at 110 deg/s times the right stick's tilt above a round deadzone of 0.51, frame-time based (measured from the view matrix)
# direct look (hle_hid.c look_cam): main 76a489f3 (2.0.1) keeps player 1's camera object's address at main+0x3561948; pitch +0xb0 / yaw +0xb4, pitch limits +0xe4 / +0xe8,
# stick lock bytes +0x121 / +0x122 (bit 6 of +0x122 ignored); 1.0.5 (main 816c5358) the same object at main+0x34513d0 (found from memory diffs around known stick turns)
# the DNS-SD service the module advertises; pack_app.py puts it and the local network text into the app's Info.plist
# the driver rewrites control +0x20..+0x27 (GLSLC's own hash) of some sections at run time (8 of the title screen's shaders came back under another key though their code was in the map):
# the key hashes those bytes as zeros, in the split and in the host
# ---- Switch 2 services the host has no device for (hle_offline.c) ----
# SDK 20.5.25's streamplay and vibration graph (nodes, players, converters) as inert stubs; only this game: they replace constructors (Mario Kart World crashed with them)
